summary: An LTP subscription on an NSE equity: Pocketful's 42-byte compact packet becomes an LTP frame; a fall decodes as a signed change; a packet cut short reaches nobody, nor does one after the unsubscribe.

notes: Frames hand-built from the decoder's offsets (packet_decoder.py:252-265); the web publishes the compact packet on the subscription's LTP topic (pocketful_adapter.py:631-642).

deviations.reason: data.mode is the label every broker's frames carry on the desktop (ltp, quote, full), as the recorded Zerodha transcripts carry it; this web adapter puts its subscription mode number there.

Pocketful sends the last trade time in epoch seconds; the web passes the seconds on as ltt (1762656900), the desktop sends epoch milliseconds (1762656900000), the unit the docs give every WebSocket time.

The web's LTP frame carries the compact packet's change; the desktop's LTP frame carries no change. The desktop decodes it as signed (-10.50 on the fall), the web unsigned (packet_decoder.py:257, '>I'), so a fall shows on the web as 42949662.46: once the desktop carries the field that push is a web defect.
The web's LTP frame carries the compact packet's open interest; the desktop's LTP frame carries none.
The web's LTP frame carries the compact packet's best bid; the desktop's common carrier drops it.
